candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance: provide age-appropriate injury-prevention and health-promotion teaching and counsel clients on behaviors that reduce preventable morbidity and mortality.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — adult motor-vehicle injury prevention and seat-belt use
candidate.educational_objective: Teach adults to use a seat belt in every seating position on every trip because consistent restraint use substantially reduces serious crash injury and death and remains necessary even with airbags.

options.A: Reserve seat-belt use mainly for highway travel because short local trips have minimal serious-injury risk.
options.B: Adults seated in the rear seat can omit seat belts when the vehicle has front and side airbags.
options.C: Wear a seat belt in every seating position on every trip, no matter how short, because consistent restraint use substantially reduces serious crash-related injury and death.
options.D: Seat belts are primarily a pediatric intervention and add little protection after a passenger reaches adulthood.

candidate.rationale: Current CDC guidance states that wearing a seat belt is the most effective way to prevent injury or death in motor-vehicle crashes for adults and older children and that seat belts reduce serious crash-related injuries and deaths by about half. CDC recommends seat-belt use in front and back seats on every trip, no matter how short, and notes that airbags provide added protection rather than replacing seat belts. Therefore C is correct. A limits use based on trip length, B incorrectly treats airbags as a substitute, and D falsely minimizes adult benefit.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Adults should wear seat belts in front and rear seating positions on every trip regardless of length; seat belts reduce serious crash-related injury/death substantially and airbags do not replace them.
